references.text: Describes Israel's settlement in Heshbon and the surrounding cities after the victory over Sihon, which Jephthah refers to.
Mentions the Arnon River as the boundary, which Jephthah also refers to in his argument.
Aroer by the Arnon Valley is mentioned as a city Israel captured, the same city that Jephthah refers to.
The tribe of Reuben built up Heshbon and other cities, confirming Israel's long-term settlement in the area.
God gave Israel Heshbon and the land of Sihon, king of the Amorites, as the basis for Jephthah's argument regarding lawful possession.
The tribe of Gad received Heshbon and half of the Ammonite territory, showing the distribution of the region that Jephthah defends.
Israel settled in the land of the Amorites after driving them out, which is the background for the 300 years that Jephthah mentions.
